chief_data.selection_justification: Candidate 4 is the only surviving design after hard-gate disqualification of candidates 1-3 due to insufficient conversion (X=0.31 < 0.50) and excessive coil length. It achieves the required selectivity advantage via enhanced laminar mixing (r_mix=0.022) and meets the minimum conversion threshold (X=0.54).
chief_data.selection_rationale: Candidate 4 is selected as the sole viable option after candidates 1, 2, and 3 were disqualified for failing the minimum conversion hard gate (X=0.31 vs required 0.50) and exceeding benchtop coil length limits. Candidate 4 achieves a conversion of 0.54, satisfying the chemistry brief's requirement for selectivity-sensitive stream logic through enhanced laminar mixing (r_mix=0.022). While its residence time (105.5 min) is longer than the ideal 3x reduction target, it is the only design that produces usable product yield in a flow format. The primary flow advantage here is selectivity control via precise mixing, rather than pure throughput. The main uncertainty is whether the estimated conversion of 0.54 is robust against minor temperature fluctuations. The first experiment should verify the conversion at the design residence time to confirm the kinetic model accuracy.
resolved_tradeoffs: id=4 vs id=1/2/3: id=4 is the only candidate meeting the X>=0.50 hard gate. id=1/2/3 were disqualified due to X=0.31 and excessive coil length.
remaining_uncertainties: Conversion estimate (X=0.54) is close to the minimum threshold; sensitivity to temperature and mixing efficiency needs verification.
Residence time distribution in the 0.75mm coil at Re=6 may be broader than ideal plug flow, potentially affecting selectivity.
chief_data.experiment_recommendation: Run reaction at design conditions (T=50C, tau=105.5 min) and measure conversion and selectivity. Compare with batch results to validate flow advantage.
